newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat continues to show improvement.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat continues to show improvement.

text.p: Condition ratings for Kansas winter wheat improved and spring planting continued to progress during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop report.
The crop was rated 11 percent excellent, 49 good, 27 fair, eight poor and five very poor. Those ratings marked the third consecutive week in which the crop showed improvement.
Statewide, 25 percent of the wheat crop was heading, below 29 percent in 1996 and the five-year average of 35 percent.
Rain is needed in the western part of the state for crop progress to continue, the report said.
Corn planting was 75 percent complete, behind 88 percent last year and the average of 71 percent.
Sorghum planting was 12 percent complete, ahead of 10 percent last year and the average of six percent.
Soybean planting was 10 percent complete, ahead of nine percent last year and six percent on average.

Topsoil moisture was three percent very short, 20 short, 69 adequate and eight percent surplus. That marked a decline from the previous week, when topsoil was rated 11 percent short, 81 percent adequate and eight percent surplus.
